question: Can the conditional generation probability of a pre-trained language model, given an instruction describing the task and aspect, serve as a training-free, customizable, multi-aspect text evaluation metric?
hypothesis: Higher-quality text of a given aspect is more likely to be generated under the context and instruction than unqualified text, so its conditional probability correlates with human judgement.
contributions: GPTScore, a training-free evaluation framework driven by task and aspect instructions with optional demonstrations
Study of 19 backbones (80M-175B) on 4 tasks, 22 aspects, 37 datasets
Observations on instruction, demonstration, aspect combination and text-davinci-003 vs 001

method.summary: The score is the mean-free sum of token log-probabilities of the hypothesis conditioned on a prompt built from a task description, an aspect definition and optional demonstrations, with equal token weights. Computed with GPT2, OPT, FLAN-T5 and GPT3 variants and compared by Spearman correlation with human ratings against ROUGE, BERTScore, MoverScore, PRISM, BARTScore, FED and DynaEval.
method.task: reference-free and reference-based NLG evaluation (summarisation, MT, data-to-text, dialogue)

datasets.name: FED (turn and dialogue level)
datasets.preprocessing: dialogue turned into Yes/No QA prompt

datasets.name: SummEval
datasets.split: sub-dataset randomly extracted for API cost; sample-level

datasets.name: BAGEL
datasets.preprocessing: named entities replaced with special tokens such as X and Y

datasets.name: MQM-2020 (zh->en)
datasets.split: samples with human scores in ACC, MQM, FLU extracted as far as possible; sample-level

models.name: ROUGE-1/2/L, BERTScore, MoverScore, PRISM, BARTScore, BARTScore+CNN, BARTScore+CNN+Para, FED, DynaEval

inference.decoding: no generation; forced-decoding log-probability of the hypothesis
inference.samples: one score per item per variant; no seeds or repeated runs stated
inference.prompting: template T(d,a,S) of task description + aspect definition + context + hypothesis; GPT3 uses OpenAI example prompts, instruction-tuned models use NaturalInstruction-style prompts; dialogue cast as Yes/No QA ending 'Answer: Yes.'; demonstrations by repeating the template; K up to 12 (MT ablation)

parameters.scoring_dimension: src->hypo for FED, SummEval/Newsroom COH/CON/INF, data-to-text, MT; ref<->hypo paraphrase prompts also listed in Table 11
parameters.demonstration_K: 0,1,2,4,8,12 in ablation; value used in main tables not stated

metrics.name: Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: rank correlation between metric score and human judgement, sample-level (mean over source texts) for summarisation, D2T, MT; dataset-level for dialogue

metrics.name: Pearson correlation
metrics.definition: linear correlation; stated as used for QXSUM in Sec 5.1

eval.protocol: Bootstrap significance test (p<0.05) of IST/IDM vs VAL (dagger) and IDM vs IST (double dagger); no repeated runs reported; sub-datasets randomly drawn due to GPT3 API cost.

prompts.text: Generate a fluent and grammatical summary for the following text: {src}\n\nTl;dr{hypo}
Generate a coherent summary for the following text: {src}\n\nTl;dr{hypo}

Answer the question based on the conversation between a human and AI.
Question: Are the responses of AI interesting? (a) Yes. (b) No.
Conversation: {History}
Answer: Yes.
Rewrite the following text with its core information and consistent facts:{ref/hypo} In other words, {hypo/ref}

evidence.quote: In our work, we treat each token equally.

results.claim: Adding instruction raises mean SummEval coherence correlation of GPTScore from 38.0 to 40.2.
results.setup: SummEval/RealSumm, sample-level Spearman, mean over 19 GPTScore variants (GPT3 x5, GPT2 x4, OPT x5, FLAN-T5 x5), VAL = no instruction, IST = task description + aspect definition, no demonstration; bootstrap significance p<0.05
results.table: Table 3, row Avg., column SummEval COH IST (VAL 38.0)

results.claim: Instruction gains on other summarisation aspects are 1-2.4 points (CON 40.4->41.4, FLU 35.8->37.2, REL 31.3->32.2, RealSumm COV 37.4->39.8).
results.setup: SummEval/RealSumm, sample-level Spearman, mean over 19 GPTScore variants (GPT3 x5, GPT2 x4, OPT x5, FLAN-T5 x5), VAL = no instruction, IST = task description + aspect definition, no demonstration; bootstrap significance p<0.05
results.table: Table 3, row Avg., column RSumm COV IST (VAL 37.4)

results.table: Table 6, FED dialogue-level, row Avg., column d01 (d03 13.5)

results.setup: FED turn-level (8 aspects), dataset-level Spearman, GPT3 variants
results.table: Table 6, FED turn-level, row Avg., column d01 (d03 32.8)

limits: Evaluation sets are random sub-samples because of GPT3 API cost; sizes of SummEval, RealSumm, NEWSROOM, MQM subsets are not given.
Only English text evaluated; cross-lingual left to future work (BLOOM).
No repeated runs or variance beyond a bootstrap test; the demonstration set and K for main tables are not stated.
Prompt engineering is left as future work; the d03 < d01 result is unexplained ('necessitating deep explorations').
Needs token log-probabilities; text-davinci-001/003 and ada-curie are retired API models.
Paper text and tables disagree in places (see results notes and problems).
